metadata.abstract: We study link prediction through the lens of the adjacency matrix. We introduce streaming modularity, which makes training substantially more stable. School of Engineering, Eastbridge University
Applied AI Laboratory, Meridian Research
Abstract

We study link prediction through the lens of the adjacency matrix. We introduce streaming modularity, which makes training substantially more stable. On PubMed, our method improves node accuracy by 6% over label propagation, while using less compute. We also analyze the role of the message passing and release our code.

blocks.text: INTRODUCTION

Recent progress in link prediction (Cohen and Zhang, 2018) has relied heavily on the message passing, yet its gradient descent remains poorly understood.1 In this paper we propose streaming modularity, a simple procedure that improves robustness to distribution shift. Our contributions are threefold: a formal treatment of the spectral filter, an efficient algorithm, and an extensive evaluation on PubMed. Recent progress in node classification (Cohen et al., 2017) has relied heavily on the community structure, yet its attention mechanism remains poorly understood.

blocks.text: RELATED WORK

Prior work on the neighborhood sampling (Ivanova, 2018; Zhang et al., 2019) assumes that the edge weight is fixed during training, which limits its flexibility. Graph Neural Network (GNN) was introduced by (Ivanova, 2019) and has since become a standard tool for link prediction. We build on the observation of (Rossi and Rossi, 2020) that a carefully chosen node embedding can substantially reduce the cost of graph classification. Unlike GCN, our approach does not require a separate embedding space and therefore removes the need for manual tuning. blocks.text: EXPERIMENTS

Compared with GraphSAGE, streaming modularity is 6% faster at inference while matching modularity. On Reddit, streaming modularity improves modularity by 14% over GraphSAGE, as reported in Table 1. Figure 1 shows that the gap in node accuracy widens as the edge weight grows, consistent with our analysis. We repeat every experiment with five random seeds and report the mean; the standard deviation is below 0.4 in all cases. DISCUSSION

Future work will explore link prediction in settings where the community structure is only partially observed. These results suggest that the node embedding is more important than previously assumed (Mehta et al., 2019; Haddad and Haddad, 2022). We hope that streaming modularity will serve as a useful baseline for further study of the community structure. These results suggest that the graph Laplacian is more important than previously assumed (Haddad and Haddad, 2022). These results suggest that the graph Laplacian is more important than previously assumed (Kaya et al., 2023). A limitation of streaming modularity is its sensitivity to the graph Laplacian, which we leave for future work.
